risks.note: Chinese manufacturers, burdened by excess capacities, directed surplus volumes into the Indian market at aggressive prices. An anti-dumping duty of USD 307 per tonne was imposed, but Chinese exporters absorbed the duty by lowering their selling prices ('anti-absorption'), negating the benefit available to domestic manufacturers. The Company applied for and the DGTR has initiated an anti-absorption investigation, and a further anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed in March 2026; both outcomes are pending, so the distortion is unresolved. As India's leading domestic insoluble sulphur manufacturer, OCCL states it 'bore the brunt of this'. [PROVENANCE: this bundle carried only the boilerplate Directors' Report risk-management-policy paragraph; the substantive risk content is back-filled from the Directors' Report OPERATIONS and FUTURE PROSPECTS sections and the Chairman's statement, which were routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles.]
risks.risk: Chinese import dumping and duty absorption in the Indian insoluble sulphur market

risks.note: Average sulphur cost rose from Rs 29 per kg to Rs 52 per kg during the year, reflecting geopolitical disruptions across global supply chains. Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, so the industry remains highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil. The Company is securing raw materials from various sources, even at a premium, and has raised inventory. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
risks.risk: Sulphur raw-material cost inflation and supply concentration in the Gulf

risks.note: Sulphur prices remained elevated while pricing flexibility in the insoluble sulphur market stayed constrained amid intense global competition, so cost pressures moved faster than realisations across parts of the market. Insoluble sulphur realisations could not increase in proportion to the rise in input costs, resulting in margin compression; profitability in FY26 was supported by the sulphuric acid business rather than the flagship product. Energy, freight and insurance costs have also risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
risks.risk: Margin compression - realisations cannot keep pace with input costs

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that 'the historically high input costs may result in demand destruction, which could negatively affect our sales volumes going forward'. Sales volume was already flat during FY26. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]
risks.risk: Demand destruction from historically high input costs

risks.note: 'In order to sustain business in this environment the Working Capital requirement has almost doubled.' risks.note: Elevated sulphur and other input prices are forcing fertilizer industries to cut production because the Government subsidy is not seen as enough to mitigate the cost increase, resulting in less demand for sulphuric acid. A subsidy revision is expected but not confirmed. This matters because the sulphuric acid and oleum business was the profit support in FY26 while insoluble sulphur margins compressed. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]
